codex-notify 1.0.0 is the first stable RubyGems.org release of the compact
Slack notification CLI for Codex.

## Highlights

- Follow new Codex JSONL activity with `codex-notify` without reposting old
  session history.
- Send Codex Hook prompts, permission requests, and final responses with
  `codex-notify-hook`, keeping one Slack thread per Codex session.
- Enable debug mode when session-start and Bash activity are intentionally
  needed.
- Resume transient Slack failures through the durable local outbox while
  preserving chunk order and stale-thread recovery behavior.
- Configure credentials and named destinations in a permission-restricted XDG
  YAML file instead of a repository.

## Security and compatibility

- Ruby 3.4 or newer is required.
- Repository `.env` files are restricted to routing and presentation settings
  by default. The temporary trusted `legacy` policy remains available for
  migration and is planned for removal in a future major release.
- Hook payloads are bounded and validated before state changes or Slack access.
- Publishing uses RubyGems Trusted Publishing through GitHub Actions OIDC; no
  long-lived RubyGems API key is used.

## Migration

Move Slack credentials to `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/codex-notify/config.yml` (or
`~/.config/codex-notify/config.yml`), replace repository credentials with a
`CODEX_NOTIFY_DESTINATION` selector, and update Codex Hook definitions to the
absolute installed path returned by `command -v codex-notify-hook`.

See [CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/koichiro/codex-notify/blob/v1.0.0/CHANGELOG.md)
and the [README](https://github.com/koichiro/codex-notify/blob/v1.0.0/README.md)
for the complete feature, security, and migration details.
